title_en: 2026 amendment of the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act and related acts

instruments.number: 令和八年法律第二十九号
instruments.name_ja: 経済社会情勢の変化を踏まえた企業の事業活動の持続的な発展を図るための産業競争力強化法等の一部を改正する法律
instruments.name_en: Act Partially Amending the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act and Other Acts

instruments.number: 令和八年政令第二百四十四号
instruments.name_ja: 経済社会情勢の変化を踏まえた企業の事業活動の持続的な発展を図るための産業競争力強化法等の一部を改正する法律の施行に伴う関係政令の整備に関する政令
instruments.name_en: Cabinet Order adjusting related Cabinet Orders for the entry into force of the amending Act

paragraphs: The bill's full title describes its aim as the sustainable development of companies' business activities in light of changes in economic and social conditions. According to the House of Councillors' summary, it amends three acts administered by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI).

Under the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act, productivity-improving equipment confirmed by the METI Minister as particularly contributing to high future productivity is defined as 'specified productivity-improving equipment', in connection with the creation of a new investment tax incentive for such equipment. New plan-certification schemes are created for business changes made in response to sudden, unforeseeable changes in international economic conditions or to rising business costs, with support such as two-step loans through the Japan Finance Corporation, and for business changes responding to falling demand for everyday goods and services caused by population decline and ageing.

Under the act on promoting regional economic driving businesses (地域経済牽引事業の促進による地域の成長発展の基盤強化に関する法律), green-space ratio rules for factories used by such businesses are relaxed further on condition that the living environment is preserved, industrial water suppliers are obliged to supply data centres within their service areas, and tax relief is provided for landowners who sell land for site development under approved plans. Under the Trade and Investment Insurance Act, insurance linked to arrangements with foreign governments that METI designates as particularly necessary for strengthening Japanese companies' supply chains becomes a separate 'specified underwriting business' with its own special account.

The Cabinet submitted the bill to the Diet on 6 March 2026. It was examined by the Committee on Economy, Trade and Industry of each House, passed by the House of Representatives on 14 May 2026 and by the House of Councillors on 29 May 2026, which enacted it. It was promulgated on 5 June 2026 as Act No. 29 of 2026.

A draft Cabinet Order adjusting related Cabinet Orders for the Act's entry into force was published for public comment on e-Gov in June 2026. The Order (Cabinet Order No. 244 of 2026) was promulgated on 31 July 2026 and amends the enforcement orders of the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act, the Trade and Investment Insurance Act and the Special Accounts Act. The Act's main provisions took effect on 31 July 2026, according to e-Gov Law Search.

confirmed.text: Article 2 and most of Article 3 of the Act (Article 3 amends the regional economic driving businesses act), together with certain supplementary provisions, take effect on a date set by Cabinet Order within six months of promulgation, under Article 1(ii) of the supplementary provisions.
The Act requires the government to review how the amended acts are working about five years after they take effect.

expected: The Cabinet Order setting the date for the second group of provisions is normally promulgated before that date.
uncertainties: When this explainer was verified, e-Gov Law Search listed the second group's effective date only as the latest date the Act allows (early December 2026), not as a date fixed by Cabinet Order.
The details of the new tax incentive are set by tax legislation and METI's confirmation procedures, which this explainer does not cover.

paragraphs: The amendment mainly creates support measures rather than new obligations for companies in general. Companies planning capital investment, or adjusting their business in response to sudden changes in international economic conditions, rising costs or shrinking local demand, may be able to apply for plan certification and the related support.

Operators of data centres and of factories in regional development projects may be affected by the industrial water and green-space rules, and companies whose supply chains rely on trade insurance linked to government-to-government arrangements may see new insurance products. Eligibility conditions are set in the acts, their enforcement orders and METI's guidance.
checklist: If you are planning capital investment in Japan, check METI's confirmation procedure for specified productivity-improving equipment and the related tax measure.
For data centre projects, check with the local industrial water supplier how the new supply obligation applies.
Watch for the Cabinet Order fixing the effective date of the second group of provisions.

review_notes: Trial explainer. Content from the House of Councillors summary; dates from the House of Representatives record and the e-Gov Law API (law_revisions/425AC0000000098 and the Act's supplementary provisions, Article 1). The METI press release URL found by search returned 404 and is not cited. The second group's date (2026-12-04 in e-Gov) is the e-Gov placeholder for 'within six months by Cabinet Order' and is not presented as a fixed date. Labelled corporate/industrial policy: the amendment is not a corporate governance reform. Re-checked 2026-10-20 (second pass): instrument numbers and formal names against e-Gov Law Search records; dates against the House of Representatives records and e-Gov revision data; content against the cited ministry and House of Councillors documents. Not yet reviewed by a person.
